newsitem.title: UK: London gold, silver poised to move higher.
newsitem.headline: London gold, silver poised to move higher.

text.p: Gold and silver showed potential to revisit stubborn price targets on Friday after easing off overnight rally highs, dealers and analysts said.
Prices had surged in New York late on Thursday, as declines in warehouse stocks and easier U.S. equity and bond markets lured investors back into commodities.
"Gold, silver and platinum are at a critical technical juncture," analyst Elli Gifford of Investment Research of Cambridge said in a commentary.
"Near term overbought, they need to extend rallies now else retreats will look likely," Gifford added.
Bullion fixed at $381.85 an ounce, little changed from the $381.75 fixing on Thursday afternoon.

Gold had hit an overnight high of $382.80 an ounce, the top level in two weeks. But selling pressure, which some dealers attributed to Australian gold miners, had pushed it back under the sticky $382 level by the time European trading started.

"The mood is not bad, the market is oversold, and if it breaks through heavy resistance at $383 it has room overhead to go to $385," a European dealer said. "But I am quite sure producers will cap the rally."
But other dealers was more bullish.
"It could be a vicious afternoon," a dealer said. "Selling's coming in at $382-$382.50, but if it's absorbed in Europe, and if the funds come in with shortcovering in New York, watch out."
Silver, boosted by recent declines in New York warehouse stocks, zoomed up past the critical $5.00 level on Thursday and hit a high bid of $5.09 overnight.
It came off the highs, but still three cents up from the close at $5.04 an ounce.
Platinum was down $1.50 at $387.25 an ounce following brisk gains earlier this week. One dealer noted that the sale of 50,000 ounces of platinum helped depress prices overnight.
